newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: OCBC reports higher profit, proposes bonus.
newsitem.headline: OCBC reports higher profit, proposes bonus.

text.p: Singapore's OCBC Bank Group reported sharply higher than expected 1996 profits on Thursday and proposed a one-for-five bonus to celebrate its 65th anniversary.
The group announced a 17.2 percent jump in net profit to Singapore $708.86 million (US$492 million) for the financial year ended December 31 1996.
The results were better than the concensus forecast of S$691.9 million by analysts in the Endinburugh Financial Publications Estimate Directory.

"It is a pretty good set of results. The bank has managed to surprise on the upside. It was our top pick for the banking sector and it continues to be the top pick," said Heath McIntyre, investment analyst with HSBC James Capel.
He said earnings growth was pretty impressive given the high base OCBC, usually seen as one of the most conservative of the four major local banks, was working from.
"The results show the earnings were mainly from its core operations," he said.
On a bank level, OCBC reported a 21.4 percent rise in net profit to S$402.64 million.
McIntyre said the only other major bank which managed to report earnings growth of more than 20 percent at the bank level was the much smaller Overseas Union Bank.
At a briefing on the OCBC group's 1996 results, a senior bank official said the loan growth for the group rose 20.6 percent to S$33.3 billion.

The official, who asked not to be identified, said strong growth was from both the bank's domestic and foreign operations. OCBC has extensive operations in Malaysia and has stepped up its presence in other markets including Australia and Hong Kong.
Overseas bank operations as a percentage of group earnings rose to 22.2 percent in 1996, up from 18.2 percent the previous year.
"A lot of the growth was from Malaysia," said the bank official, who added that he expected the rise in overseas operations to continue.
He also said the group would not reopen merger talks with Malaysian's Pacific Bank Bhd called off earlier in January.
OCBC would soon start joint venture operations in Indonesia with PT Bank NISP, but contributions were not expected for three to five years, he said.

On the property front, the group saw good contribution from its Country Side residential project in Singapore. The banks earnings from property were included under other income, which rose 16.1 percent to S$217.17.
On prospects for the current year, the bank official said: "If we are lucky, we will be able to see double digit growth."
On the bank's outlook on interest rates, he said: "The quarter percent hike by the Federal Reserve has not made much impact on our interest rates."
